title: Positive cubature on $S^2$:low-degree rigidity and uniform bounds
summary: Let \(N_t\) denote the least number of nodes in a positive cubature formula of degree \(t\) on \(S^2\). We prove that a formula of degree \(2m+1\) cannot have exactly \((m+1)(m+2)+1\) nodes for any \(m\ge2\). Excluding equality in the Fisher bound then gives \[ N_{2m+1}\ge (m+1)(m+2)+2 \] for \(m\ge3\), and known constructions yield the exact values \(N_7=22\) and \(N_9=32\). For general odd degrees, positive circle measures on Lobatto latitudes give an upper bound with quadratic coefficient \(13/8\), parity-dependent linear terms, and an \(O(m^{2/3})\) remainder.
